title: Non-Executing Security Analysis of AI Model Supply-Chain Artifacts
subtitle: Provenance, Serialization, Impersonation, and Repository Risk Inspection
contribution: A primarily non-executing model-artifact security scanner combining static code analysis, symbolic and taint-style inspection, binary-format parsing, provenance checks, and fail-loud handling of incomplete analysis before model loading.
methods: Apply AST, pattern, symbolic, taint-style, metadata, and provenance checks.
Reject unsafe dynamic-execution paths in the scanner itself.
Emit findings and fail-loud states for incomplete or unsafe analysis.
evidence: Cited Python 3.12 CI: 241 passed, 1 skipped, 6 additional subtests; 75.67% statement coverage; 75% configured gate.
Static inspection supports SafeTensors, GGUF, ONNX, Keras and pickle-derived artifacts, plus AST, symbolic, taint-style and dependency/provenance checks.

Separate guarded offline harness: 12 attack fixtures + 18 variants + 3 large-artifact assertions detected; 4 benign samples produced no actionable findings. Network/subprocess calls were denied and report writing disabled.
Fixture labels are incident-inspired regression data; external incident/CVE correctness was not independently authenticated.
limitations: Static analysis does not prove model safety or generally detect neural-weight backdoors.
Fixture detections are not population precision/recall; four benign samples do not establish a universal false-positive rate.
Unsupported or incomplete analysis must remain explicit; no untrusted model code was executed in this verification.
reproduction: Install the documented development extras and run python -m pytest tests/ -q using the cited Linux CI configuration.
A different platform or dependency set may produce different counts/coverage. This poster is not a promise about the latest main.
